description: Published forecasts about AI's future. A forecast appears in a simulated history only where it is compatible with that history: from its forecast year, at the first year its conditions hold (its technology reached; any world measures met), and only if that is no later than year + windowYears and before the history ends. techId is the technology drawn as its cause (it may be a technology of the real past); null means no arrow.

forecasts.label:
The Superhuman
Coder
forecasts.note: The AI 2027 scenario (Daniel Kokotajlo, Scott Alexander and colleagues, 2025) forecasts an AI that codes better than the best human engineers by 2027, setting off an intelligence explosion.

forecasts.label:
The $100-Billion
Cluster
forecasts.note: Situational Awareness (2024) projects training clusters costing over $100 billion and drawing around 10 gigawatts by about 2028, and a trillion-dollar cluster by 2030.

forecasts.label:
Three Mile Island
Restarts for AI
forecasts.note: Under a 20-year deal signed in 2024, Constellation Energy plans to restart the Three Mile Island Unit 1 reactor, renamed the Crane Clean Energy Center, to power Microsoft's data centres.

forecasts.label:
A Machine Passes
the Turing Test
forecasts.note: Ray Kurzweil has predicted since 1999 that a computer will pass a valid Turing test by 2029, and repeated it in The Singularity Is Nearer (2024).

forecasts.label:
A Fault-Tolerant
Quantum Computer
forecasts.note: IBM plans Starling, a large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computer with about 200 logical qubits, for 2029.

forecasts.label:
Data Centres Double
Their Power Use
forecasts.note: The IEA's Energy and AI report (2025) projects that data centres' electricity use will more than double by 2030, to around 945 terawatt-hours, driven mainly by AI.

forecasts.label:
The 10,000× Training
Run
forecasts.note: Epoch AI (2024) estimates that training runs around 10,000 times larger than GPT-4's, about 2×10²⁹ operations, can be feasible by 2030 if power and chips keep up.

forecasts.label:
300 Million Jobs
Exposed
forecasts.note: Goldman Sachs economists estimated in 2023 that generative AI could expose the equivalent of 300 million full-time jobs to automation.

forecasts.label:
A Century of Biology
in a Decade
forecasts.note: In Machines of Loving Grace (2024), Anthropic's chief executive argues that powerful AI could compress 50 to 100 years of biological and medical progress into 5 to 10 years.

forecasts.label:
Half of All Work
Automated
forecasts.note: McKinsey (2023) estimates that half of today's work activities could be automated between 2030 and 2060, with a midpoint around 2045.

forecasts.label: The Singularity
forecasts.note: Kurzweil dates the Singularity to 2045: people merge with the AI they have built and multiply their intelligence a millionfold (The Singularity Is Near, 2005; The Singularity Is Nearer, 2024).

forecasts.label:
Machines Outperform
Humans at Every Task
forecasts.note: In the largest survey of AI researchers (Grace et al., 2024), the aggregate forecast gives a 50% chance that unaided machines outperform humans at every task by 2047.

forecasts.label:
The Extinction
Odds Rise
forecasts.note: Geoffrey Hinton said in December 2024 that there is a 10 to 20 per cent chance AI leads to human extinction within thirty years. In this history the game's AI-risk measure crosses 75 of 100 within that window.
